## In two minutes

`copilot-fanout-lab` is an experiment repository, not a deployed product: it tests whether a coding agent can analyse a codebase one component at a time, one pull request per component, with several passes per pull request and a way to stop and ask the team (`README.md:3-5`). It holds a tiny sample shop and the scripts that drive the experiment. The shop is two Python libraries: `catalog`, an in-memory table of three products with price, stock and image lookups plus a supplier feed refresher, and `orders`, which totals an order with one discount, validates its lines against stock and posts a settled order to a payment partner (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-47`, `components/orders/orders.py:19-51`). The `tools` component has three scripts: `plan.py` writes an inventory to `codebase-analysis/plan.json`, `fanout.sh` opens one GitHub issue per component, and `gate.py` checks each pass of a component's analysis against that inventory (`tools/plan.py:1-6`, `tools/fanout.sh:2-5`, `tools/gate.py:1-12`). The code imports only the Python 3 standard library and its own modules, plus bash and the `gh` command (every `import` line in `components` and `tools`, listed in `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`, Dependencies); nothing is deployed and nothing listens on a port (search `socket`, `listen`, `serve`, `flask` in `*.py` and `*.sh`: 0 hits). The only data is a dict in memory and the plan file. Three things matter most for whoever works on it next. First, the settlement call to the payment partner uses plain `http` with no authentication, and the team has not said whether that is to stay (`components/orders/orders.py:7-9`, `Q-001`). Second, `fetch_supplier_feed`, `apply_feed`, `order_total`, `validate` and `settle` have no caller in the repository, so how they are used is unknown (`Q-002`, `Q-003`). Third, tests cover one function per component and nothing in `tools` (`components/orders/test_orders.py:7-8`, `components/catalog/test_catalog.py:7-8`).

# Architecture

The system is a Python 3 standard-library codebase with no server, no database and no deployed unit. It has two library components, `catalog` and `orders`, where `orders` imports `catalog` (`components/orders/orders.py:5`), and one tools component of three command-line scripts around a shared file, `codebase-analysis/plan.json` (`tools/plan.py:55-57`, `tools/gate.py:86`, `tools/fanout.sh:9`). Running it means running a script or the unit tests; nothing starts on its own (listing of the repository: no Dockerfile, compose file, chart, Terraform, `requirements` file or `pyproject.toml`).

Trigger: a caller, not in the repository, calls `fetch_supplier_feed` and then `apply_feed`; the docstring says this runs nightly from cron (`components/catalog/catalog.py:37`, `Q-002`). Outcome: prices and stock of known SKUs replaced.

# Cross-cutting concerns

Each section says what the system does in plain words. The system is small, so most concerns are "absent" in the code; that is a finding, not a gap in the analysis.

## Authentication and authorisation

The Python code authenticates nothing: no function checks who calls it, and the two outbound HTTP calls send no authentication header (`components/orders/orders.py:49`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:38`; search `Authorization`, `Bearer`, `jwt`, `api_key` in `*.py` and `*.sh`: 0 hits). The access control found is outside the code (search `Authorization`, `Bearer`, `jwt`, `api_key` in `*.py` and `*.sh`: 0 hits): the `claude.yml` workflow reacts only to comments by an owner, member or collaborator (`.github/workflows/claude.yml:11-13`), and `fanout.sh` relies on the operator's own `gh` login (assumed).

Consistency: absent in the code.

## Secrets

No secret appears in the code, and none is read from the environment by it. The `claude.yml` workflow reads two repository secrets by name, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and runs the Claude action only when one of them is set (`.github/workflows/claude.yml:29-34`, `.github/workflows/claude.yml:40-44`). Values are never written in this analysis.

Consistency: same everywhere (nothing stored in the repository).

## Configuration

Configuration is constants in source files and one environment variable. The URLs and discount rates are module constants (`components/orders/orders.py:9-16`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:5-6`); `ENGINE` is the one environment variable (`tools/fanout.sh:8`). There are no environments or profiles; the `dev` argument of `settle` selects a local fake address at call time (`components/orders/orders.py:47`). See `reference/configuration.md`.

Consistency: varies (2 variants): constants in the library, an environment variable and arguments in the tools.

## Error handling

Errors are mostly not handled. The library raises `KeyError` for an unknown SKU and lets `urllib` and `json` errors escape (`components/catalog/catalog.py:22-23`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:36-39`, `components/orders/orders.py:50`). `validate` is the one function that turns bad input into values, a list of messages (`components/orders/orders.py:35-42`). The tools report failure as printed `FAIL:` lines and exit code 1, and `gate.py` handles bad `status.json` explicitly (`tools/gate.py:23-26`, `tools/gate.py:95-103`); `fanout.sh` stops at the first failure and exits 2 for an unknown engine (`tools/fanout.sh:6`, `tools/fanout.sh:29`).

Consistency: varies (3 variants): exceptions in the library, messages in `validate`, exit codes in the tools.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | exceptions propagate | `components/catalog/catalog.py:23`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:36-39` |
| `orders` | exceptions propagate, except `validate` which returns messages | `components/orders/orders.py:25`, `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` |
| `tools` | printed FAIL lines and exit codes | `tools/gate.py:23-26`, `tools/fanout.sh:29` |

## Resilience

There is none: no retry, circuit breaker, fallback or queue. Both HTTP calls have a timeout (15 seconds for `settle`, 10 for the feed) and nothing else (`components/orders/orders.py:45`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:36`; search `retry`, `backoff`, `circuit` in `*.py` and `*.sh`: 0 hits). `apply_feed` is not atomic, so a bad feed item leaves earlier items applied (`components/catalog/catalog.py:44-47`). `fanout.sh` is not idempotent for issues (`tools/fanout.sh:25-28`). The pass 3 test run in `gate.py` has no timeout (`tools/gate.py:73-75`).

Consistency: absent.

## Logging, metrics and tracing

No logging, metrics or tracing in the code (search `logging`, `print(` in `components`: 0 hits; `print` in `tools`: the result lines of `gate.py` and `plan.py`, `tools/gate.py:25`, `tools/gate.py:111`, `tools/plan.py:58`). There is no health check or dashboard. The Claude workflow echoes that a mention reached Actions (`.github/workflows/claude.yml:25-26`).

Consistency: absent in the library; printed result lines only in the tools.

## Build and deployment

There is nothing to build or deploy: no package file, no container, no release step (listing of the repository: none). CI runs the scripts on GitHub-hosted runners with Python 3.12 (`.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml:10-17`, `.github/workflows/toolkit-analysis.yml:13-18`). `plan.yml` commits `codebase-analysis/plan.json` to the repository with a bot identity when it changed (`.github/workflows/plan.yml:15-24`). The pipeline is drawn in `hld/02-architecture.md`.

Consistency: same everywhere (CI only).

## Testing

Two unittest files, one test each, `line_total("SKU-3", 2)` and `price_of("SKU-1")` (`components/orders/test_orders.py:7-8`, `components/catalog/test_catalog.py:7-8`). No test touches discounts, validation, settlement, the feed or any of the tools (inferred: only those calls appear in the two test files). The gate's pass 3 runs the whole suite with `python -m unittest discover` (`tools/gate.py:73-75`), and the repository instructions give the same command (`.github/copilot-instructions.md:5-6`). No network is used by the tests (inferred: `settle` and `fetch_supplier_feed` are not called by them).

Consistency: same everywhere (one-test files in each component, none in `tools`).

## Dependencies

No third-party Python package is used: every import is standard library or a repository module (imports at `components/orders/orders.py:2-5`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:2-3`, `tools/gate.py:13-18`, `tools/plan.py:8-15`). External programs: `gh` and `python3` for `fanout.sh` (`tools/fanout.sh:9-10`). CI uses four GitHub Actions at fixed major versions (`.github/workflows/toolkit-analysis.yml:15-16`, `.github/workflows/toolkit-analysis.yml:28`, `.github/workflows/claude.yml:40`).

Consistency: same everywhere.

Generated from the analysis of 2026-11-21, depth deep. The code is the source of truth: open the cited lines before acting on any statement here.

Limits of the graph and chunks: calls through dynamic dispatch, callbacks, reflection, string-built names or another language are not in the graph, so an absent `CALLS` edge is not proof of no call. `name-unique` and `analysis` edges are leads to check. ## What the system is

An experiment repository that tests component-by-component code analysis by a coding agent (`README.md:3-5`). It has a sample shop of two Python libraries, `catalog` and `orders`, and `tools`, three scripts that write an inventory (`plan.py`), open one issue per component (`fanout.sh`) and gate each analysis pass (`gate.py`). It is Python 3 standard library plus bash, has no server and no database, and runs from a checkout or a GitHub Actions runner (`tools/plan.py:61-62`, `tools/gate.py:116-117`, `tools/fanout.sh:3`). Its only data is `_PRODUCTS`, a dict in memory (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12`), and `codebase-analysis/plan.json` (`tools/plan.py:55-57`).

## Domain vocabulary

- SKU: product key such as `SKU-1`, the key of `_PRODUCTS` (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12`).
- line: one `(sku, qty)` pair of an order (`components/orders/orders.py:24`).
- loyal: flag giving the 5 percent loyalty discount (`components/orders/orders.py:14`, `components/orders/orders.py:28-29`).

# Risks and surprises

What a new engineer must be warned about, ordered by impact: security, data loss, outages, wrong results, maintainability. Each row names the page that has the detail.

| # | What | Why it matters | Evidence | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The payment partner address is plain `http`, and `settle` sends order id and amount with no authentication header | Order and amount travel unencrypted and unauthenticated; the comment says the partner plans TLS without a date (`Q-001`) | `components/orders/orders.py:7-9`, `components/orders/orders.py:48-50` | [orders](../lld/orders/orders.md), `hld/03-integrations.md` |
| 2 | The supplier feed address is plain `http`, and the feed is applied with no signature or schema check | A person in the path could change prices and stock | `components/catalog/catalog.py:5`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:36-47` | [catalog](../lld/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 3 | `apply_feed` is not atomic: an item without `price` or `stock`, or with a non-numeric value, raises after earlier items were applied | A bad feed leaves the product table half updated | `components/catalog/catalog.py:44-47` | [catalog](../lld/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 4 | `settle` has no retry, no idempotency key and no handling of errors; a timeout does not say whether the partner processed the order | A caller that retries after a timeout may settle twice (inferred: no key in the body at `components/orders/orders.py:48`) | `components/orders/orders.py:45-51` | [orders](../lld/orders/orders.md) |
| 5 | `validate` is not called by `order_total` or `settle`, and no caller in the repository calls them | A negative quantity lowers a total; an unknown SKU raises `KeyError` in pricing (`Q-003`) | `components/orders/orders.py:23-32`, `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` | [orders](../lld/orders/orders.md) |
| 6 | `fetch_supplier_feed` is documented as nightly from cron, but nothing schedules it or calls `apply_feed` (`Q-002`) | Prices and stock may never refresh | `components/catalog/catalog.py:37` | [catalog](../lld/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 7 | `get_product` returns the live record | A caller that edits the returned dict changes the catalog | `components/catalog/catalog.py:17` | [catalog](../lld/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 8 | `in_stock` gives `False` for an unknown SKU and for too little stock, so `validate` reports both as "not enough stock"; `in_stock` with `qty` of zero or less is always true for a known SKU | The caller cannot tell a typo from a sold-out product | `components/catalog/catalog.py:29`, `components/orders/orders.py:40-41` | [catalog](../lld/catalog/catalog.md), [orders](../lld/orders/orders.md) |
| 9 | `plan.py` recounts `test_count` on every run, which moves the baseline of gate pass 3 | Running it after tests were added removes the "new tests" check | `tools/plan.py:3-5`, `tools/plan.py:36`, `tools/gate.py:69-72` | [plan](../lld/tools/plan.md) |
| 10 | The gate's ASK message tells the reader to wait for an answer in `decisions.md`, a file the gate never reads | The message points to a place the check does not use | `tools/gate.py:60` | [gate](../lld/tools/gate.md) |
| 11 | Pass numbers other than 1, 2 and 3 pass silently, and the pass 3 check runs the whole repository's tests | A typo such as `--pass 4` prints PASS; a failing test in another component fails this component's pass 3 | `tools/gate.py:45-78`, `tools/gate.py:73-75` | [gate](../lld/tools/gate.md) |
| 12 | `fanout.sh` creates issues again on every run, and an unknown `ENGINE` is noticed only after labels were made | Duplicate issues; partial side effects | `tools/fanout.sh:10-12`, `tools/fanout.sh:25-29` | [fanout](../lld/tools/fanout.md) |
| 13 | Two documents that act disagree on where analysis output goes: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the `component-analysis` skill say `codebase-analysis/components/<name>/`, while the issue for this book says `bible/` | An agent that follows the wrong one writes in the wrong place; the PR scope check accepts `bible/` as a separate "book" component | `.github/copilot-instructions.md:3-4`, `.github/skills/component-analysis/SKILL.md:16-17`, `.github/workflows/analysis-gate.yml:28-29` | `run-notes.md` |
| 14 | The repository README says the settlement URL should make pass 2 stop and ask; the code comment is the only place that explains the URL | The reason is a comment, not a decision record | `README.md:12-13`, `components/orders/orders.py:7-9` | [orders](../lld/orders/orders.md) |
| 15 | Both `http://partner-legacy.internal/settle` and the developer-only `http://localhost:8099/settle` appear in the plan as sites to classify, because the pattern cannot tell them apart | Pass 2 must classify a developer fake as if it were deployed | `tools/plan.py:18`, `codebase-analysis/plan.json:76-85` | [plan](../lld/tools/plan.md) |
| 16 | The tools component has no tests, and the library has one test per component | Discounts, validation, settlement, the feed and every gate rule are untested | `components/orders/test_orders.py:7-8`, `components/catalog/test_catalog.py:7-8` | [tools](../lld/tools/README.md) |
